knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.3.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly recovers unconditional mean and variance by conditioning on X?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the tower and total-variance identities.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The tower property averages conditional means. Total variance adds average within-condition variance and variance between conditional means.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Stopping at a conditional quantity without the outer expectation or omitting one variance component.

choices.label: E[Y]=E[Y|X] for every realised X, so no outer expectation is required.
Var(Y)=Var(E[Y|X]) only, because conditional variation disappears after conditioning.
Var(Y)=E[Var(Y|X)] only, because variation of conditional means is irrelevant.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.3.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. P(X=1)=0.4, E[Y|X=0]=10, and E[Y|X=1]=20. What is E[Y]?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The outer expectation weights each conditional mean by the probability of its condition.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Stopping at E[Y|X] or averaging conditional means without probability weights.

choices.label: E[Y]=20 because E[Y|X=1] is the conditional mean for the event explicitly given.
E[Y]=(10+20)/2=15 because conditional means always receive equal weight.
E[Y]=E[Y|X], so the answer remains the two-valued function 10 or 20 rather than one unconditional mean.

worked_example.title: Tower law and variance decomposition for claim cost
worked_example.problem_statement: A risk type indicator X equals 0 with probability 0.4 and 1 with probability 0.6. Conditional on X, claim cost Y (£00) satisfies E[Y | X = 0] = 5, E[Y | X = 1] = 12, Var(Y | X = 0) = 4, and Var(Y | X = 1) = 9. Compute E[Y] and Var(Y) using the conditioning formulae.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Apply E[Y] = E[E[Y|X]], then Var(Y) = E[Var(Y|X)] + Var(E[Y|X]).

steps.label: Apply the tower law for the mean
steps.attempt_cue: Average the conditional means with P(X).
steps.explanation: The law of total expectation recovers the unconditional mean from the conditional means.

steps.label: Form E[Var(Y|X)] and Var(E[Y|X])
steps.attempt_cue: Average the conditional variances, then variance the conditional means.
steps.explanation: Within-group variation is E[Var(Y|X)]. Between-group variation is Var(E[Y|X]) = E[m(X)²] − (E[m(X)])² with m(X) = E[Y|X].

steps.label: Add for Var(Y) and refuse stopping at E[Y|X]
steps.attempt_cue: Sum the two variance pieces and state why E[Y|X] alone is incomplete.
steps.explanation: Total variance is within plus between. Stopping after reporting E[Y|X] leaves both the unconditional mean (unless averaged) and the variance decomposition unfinished.

worked_example.final_answer: E[Y] = 9.2; Var(Y) = 18.76, from E[Var(Y|X)] = 7 and Var(E[Y|X]) = 11.76.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Reporting only E[Y|X] = 5 or 12 as if that finished the mean, or computing Var(Y) as E[Var(Y|X)] = 7 and omitting the between-group term Var(E[Y|X]) = 11.76.
